method: Yarn count systems are either direct - mass per length, so a larger number is thicker - or indirect - length per mass, so a larger number is finer. Tex is grams per 1,000 m, so decitex is ten times the tex value and denier is nine times it, and every entry is converted through tex. An indirect count C is the number of hanks of its own length that weigh one pound, so its tex equivalent is 1,000 x 453.59237 / (hanks x yardsPerHank x 0.9144) / C: 1,000 for the metric count (1 km per kg), and 590.541, 885.812, 310.034 and 1,653.515 per unit of count for the cotton (840 yd), worsted (560 yd), woolen run (1,600 yd) and linen (300 yd) hanks. Both 0.9144 m per yard and 453.59237 g per pound are exact definitions, so those factors are computed from them rather than transcribed, and they agree with the six-figure factors in ASTM D2260 (0.590541, 0.885812, 0.310034 and 1.65352). The ply field multiplies the mass per length by the number of plies, which is the same as dividing an indirect count, so 2/28 Nm is two plies of 28 Nm and behaves as 14 Nm or 71.4 tex. Results are rounded half up to three significant figures, with a billionth of slack added before rounding so a value that should land exactly on a half rounds up rather than down. Counts are accepted for yarns from 0.01 to 10,000 tex (0.09 to 90,000 denier), and that range test allows a billionth of relative slack so a boundary written in another unit, such as 0.09 denier, is not refused because of binary representation error. Twists, retraction and shrinkage are out of scope: twisting takes up length, so a real plied yarn can be slightly finer than the arithmetic resultant, and a count is a nominal linear density rather than a measured diameter, so the tool does not estimate yarn thickness, gauge or fabric sett. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: ASTM D2260-03(2013), Standard Tables of Conversion Factors and Equivalent Yarn Numbers Measured in Various Numbering Systems: the tex, denier, cotton, worsted, woolen run, metric and linen systems with their 0.590541, 0.885812, 0.310034 and 1.65352 factors.
ISO 1144, Textiles - Universal system for designating linear density (Tex system): tex as grams per 1,000 m with decitex and its multiples.
ISO 2060, Textiles - Yarn from packages - Determination of linear density (mass per unit length) by the skein method: linear density measured as mass per unit length.
International yard and pound agreement (1959): one yard is exactly 0.9144 m and one pound is exactly 453.59237 g.

Textile trade yarn-numbering references (for example the Swicofil yarn manual): cotton count 840 yd per pound, worsted count 560 yd, woolen run 1,600 yd and linen count 300 yd, and the count/ply conventions for folded yarns.
